title: Trade-Based Money Laundering: Detection and Investigation
summary: A six-module programme equipping customs, FIU and law-enforcement officers to detect and investigate trade-based money laundering using trade and financial data.
intro: This training programme equips customs, FIU and law-enforcement officers to detect and investigate trade-based money laundering by analysing trade and financial data, recognising mis-invoicing and other red flags, and working across agencies.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give customs officers, FIU analysts and investigators a practical understanding of how international trade is used to move value and disguise criminal proceeds. Participants leave able to spot the red flags in trade and financial data, target high-risk traders and consignments, and build joint cases with FIU, tax and law-enforcement partners.
sections.What It Covers: How trade-based money laundering works, trade documentation and trade finance, customs data, mis-invoicing and misdescription of goods, phantom and multiple shipments, red-flag indicators and data analysis, free trade zones, and cooperation with FIUs, tax authorities and foreign customs.
Intended Audience: Customs officers, trade intelligence analysts and post-clearance audit teams
FIU analysts and financial investigators handling trade-related intelligence
Tax investigators and prosecutors working on trade-linked fraud and laundering cases
Learning Objectives: Explain how trade transactions are used to move value and launder proceeds
Interpret customs declarations, trade documents and trade finance records
Identify mis-invoicing, misdescription and other red flags in trade and financial data
Assess the vulnerabilities of free trade zones and transhipment
Analyse trade data to target high-risk traders and consignments
Build joint investigations with FIUs, tax authorities and foreign partners
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with trade-document exercises and data analysis, ending in a case workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the participants' agencies and trade profile.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of customs, financial intelligence or financial crime investigation is helpful. No specialist knowledge of trade finance is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2010), Money Laundering Vulnerabilities of Free Trade Zones
FATF and Egmont Group (2020), Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments
FATF and Egmont Group (2021), Trade-Based Money Laundering: Risk Indicators

modules.title: Trade-Based Money Laundering: How It Works
modules.summary: How international trade is used to transfer value and disguise criminal proceeds, why it is hard to detect, and how it links to drugs, fraud, sanctions evasion and informal value transfer.
objectives: Explain the basic mechanics of value transfer through trade
Identify the predicate crimes and actors most associated with trade-based laundering
Recognise why trade-based laundering is hard to detect
syllabus: Trade as a means of moving value across borders
Links to drugs, fraud, customs and tax offences and sanctions evasion
Informal value transfer and trade settlement
FATF and Egmont Group findings on trends and developments

modules.title: Trade Documentation, Trade Finance and Customs Data
modules.summary: The documents and data generated by international trade, from invoices and transport documents to letters of credit and customs declarations, and what each can reveal to an investigator.
objectives: Read the core trade documents and customs declarations
Explain open-account trade and documentary trade finance
Identify which agency or firm holds which trade and payment records
syllabus: Commercial invoices, packing lists and bills of lading
Customs declarations, tariff classification and valuation
Open account, letters of credit and documentary collections
Where the data sits: customs, banks, carriers and FIUs

modules.title: Mis-Invoicing and Other Techniques
modules.summary: The main techniques identified in international typologies, including over- and under-invoicing, multiple invoicing, misdescription of goods and phantom shipments, and how each shows up in the data.
objectives: Explain over- and under-invoicing and their financial effect
Recognise multiple invoicing, misdescription and phantom shipments
Distinguish trade-based laundering from customs fraud and commercial error
syllabus: Over- and under-invoicing of goods and services
Multiple invoicing and over- or under-shipment
Misdescription, misclassification and phantom shipments
Service-based and high-value goods schemes

modules.title: Red Flags, Data Analysis and Free Trade Zones
modules.summary: How customs and FIUs use risk indicators and data analytics to identify suspicious trade, and the particular vulnerabilities of free trade zones and transhipment hubs.
objectives: Apply trade-based laundering red-flag indicators to cases
Use price, volume and route analysis to identify anomalies
Assess the risks posed by free trade zones and transhipment
syllabus: Risk indicators for traders, goods, routes and payments
Unit-price analysis, mirror trade data and data matching
Free trade zones: oversight gaps and risk indicators
Risk targeting and selection for examination

modules.title: Joint Investigation with FIUs, Tax and Foreign Partners
modules.summary: How to turn trade anomalies into cases by combining customs, financial and tax information, using domestic gateways and international cooperation between customs administrations, FIUs and tax authorities.
objectives: Combine customs, financial and tax information lawfully
Use international customs, FIU and tax cooperation channels
Plan a joint investigation with clear roles and objectives
syllabus: Domestic gateways and joint task forces
Exchange of trade data and customs mutual assistance
FIU and tax information exchange channels
Evidencing value transfer for prosecution and recovery

modules.title: Case Workshop: Investigating a Trade-Based Scheme
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams analyse trade documents and payment data, identify the laundering technique and agree a joint investigation and enforcement plan.
objectives: Apply red flags and data analysis to a realistic case
Identify evidential gaps and how to fill them
Agree a coordinated enforcement and recovery response
syllabus: Case briefing: a multi-country trade and payment scheme
Document and data analysis exercise
Evidence, charges and asset recovery options
Workshop: the joint investigation plan

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.
